chunks: From him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi, who said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and with us was Abu Basir and some people from the Mountains, asking him about the sacrifices of the People of the Book. He said to them, 'You have heard what Allah, the Exalted, said in His Book.' They said to him, 'We would like you to inform us [explicitly].' He said, 'Do not eat them.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ: People of the Book (Jews and Christians)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating the sacrifices of the People of the Book according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) directs the questioners to the Quranic verse regarding the food of the People of the Book, yet when pressed for a direct ruling, he explicitly commands 'Do not eat them.' This indicates a position of caution or prohibition (likely *karaahat tanzeehi* or *haram* depending on the school of thought) distinct from the general permissibility derived from Surah Al-Ma'idah, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the specific context of 'food' (*ta'am*) as including sacrifices. The dialogue highlights the methodological nuance where the Imam uses the Quran as the primary evidence before providing a definitive practical ruling to his companions.
